text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Government chose capitals for the five new consolidated provinces: Mikkeli, Hameenlinna, Turku, Oulu and Rovaniemi.
- Merger talks between Merita Bank and insurer Sampo failed in January.
- The Pritzkers, American owners of Hyatt hotels, claim tens of millions of markka from troubled SKOPBANK, which their lawyers say illegally forced Hyatt out of the Virgin Islands.
- Central Union of Agricultural Producers MTK wants to slow down development of EU's Natura protected lands network.
- Local strike at small paper maker in Kotka threatening to expand to bigger pulp and paper mills next week.
- Sami people celebrate their national day today -- Sami community in Helsinki 400-500 strong.
- International Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) planning easier criteria for environmental labelling for paper and pulp mills that buy timber from many sellers.
- Insurance group Sampo and its associates Elake-Varma and Yrittajain Fennia have combined their real estate management in Kiinteistovarma Oy which manages property worth 17 billion markka.
- Finnish boat business is recovering from recession and profitability has improved, but sales still lower than 1989-90 peak years.
- Finnlines CEO Antti Lageroos said trade unions the biggest problem in Finnish and Swedish ports where working day is just four hours.
- Joining NATO would pose a risk to Finland's sovereignty, says peace researcher Arto Nokkala.
- One in every six female workers in parliament says she has experienced some form of sexual harassment, a survey shows.
- Finland should seek NATO membership alongside Sweden so they can form a common Nordic front, says Professor Krister Stahlberg of Abo Academy.
